_comment: "Open a JSON and the verdict changes" demo: a copy of config/policy.json with the escalation threshold of hardcoded_secret at 0.95. Copy it to ~/.config/jev-hooks/policy.json (user layer, trusted, applies in full): the demo diff secret.diff goes from NITS with an escalation to MERGE, and the hook lets the commit through on the first attempt.

lanes.name: BLOCK
lanes._rules: No model rule: BLOCK comes only from the detectors' floors (keys with a production prefix, private keys). If you want the model to block on its own, add a rule here in your own ~/.config/jev-hooks/policy.json.

lanes.name: SECURITY REVIEW
lanes._rules: No model rule: SECURITY REVIEW comes from the detectors' floors (text addressed to the reviewer, delimiters, bidirectional controls, reviewer rules). The lane stays for whoever wants a model rule in it, in the user file.

lanes.name: NITS

rules._why: Demo threshold: the plugin's is lower (see the _why of the same rule in config/policy.json). The secret in secret.diff scores 0.874: with 0.95 it stays below, and the question does not go to Claude (MERGE).

Choice c_scelta, 1 − P(none): negatives reach above 0.99, which is why the threshold is this high. Dev: TPR 1.00 (8/8), FPR 0.036 (4/110), with the four false alarms between 0.995 and 0.997 and the positives above 0.998: going higher would mean chasing the dev set. Holdout: TPR 0.83 (10/12, two positives missed at 0.960 and 0.989), FPR 0.064 (7/109). The unless on docs_only came from live use (2026-10-03): a commit of three Markdown files that described a front-end script scored 0.996 and was escalated, while an injection needs code the program runs. The bench numbers are the same with and without it. A real commit of a front-end script at 0.997, with every innerHTML value escaped or numeric, stays escalated: 0.998 would keep every dev positive but lose the holdout's positive at 0.994.

Choice c_scelta, 1 − P(none). Dev: TPR 1.00 (9/9), FPR 0.028 (3/109). Holdout: TPR 1.00 (12/12), FPR 0.037 (4/109). Raised from 0.20 after live use (2026-09-28): the question fired on every commit that added or tightened tests, at 0.25 to 0.86, with the model picking ci_tests_off or test_removed on diffs with no CI file and no removed line. At 0.20 the holdout FPR was 0.083 (9/109), six of the nine false alarms between 0.22 and 0.70; 0.50 keeps every positive on both sets. Above the threshold the question goes to Claude, who looks at the tests and does not block. The unless on docs_only came from live use (2026-09-28): two documentation-only commits scored 0.25 and 0.28 and were escalated, while a diff of documentation files alone cannot remove, skip or loosen a test. The bench numbers are the same with and without it. The unless on weakens_expected (2026-09-29) asks a second reading, the i_expected wording, and escalates only when both see a weakening: on a fresh holdout written blind (bench/results/2026-09-29-holdout-weakens) the pair keeps 15 of 16 positives, as the rule alone, with 4 false alarms in 44 instead of 10; on live.jsonl 4 in 17 instead of 9; on dev and on the old holdout the same counts as the rule alone. A missing weakens_expected answer leaves the rule firing. The unless on touches_tests (2026-10-04) came from live use: a commit that deleted three Vue components and touched no test scored 0.55, with the second reading at 0.57, while every weakening the bench defines needs a test, CI or test-tool file in the diff. On the bench no positive lacks one (47 of 47 keep the rule) and the numbers are the same with and without it, since the bench's false alarms all touch tests; on 88 reviewed commits of other repositories it removes one of the four false weakens_tests escalations. Since 2026-10-07 both readings count only the chunks that hold a test, CI or test-tool file (chunks_matching in checks.json): the threshold and the conditions are the same, and on 126 real multi-chunk commits with no weakening the false escalations drop from 28 to 17. Raised from 0.10 to 0.30 on 2026-10-07, once the measurement recorded the option each chunk picks: in 12 of the 14 real false escalations left the second reading picked none, at 0.12 to 0.30. Real multi-chunk commits 16 to 4 false escalations, split bench diffs 4 to 1 of 126, dev 3 to 2 of 109, live 3 to 0 of 17 (simulate-policy), the blind holdout 4 of 44 with 15 of 16 positives at both thresholds. The cost: on the old holdout (bench/results/2026-09-28-holdout-i_expected, the same wording measured under the weakens_tests name) a positive that marks a test xfail scores 0.179, so 11 of 12 positives instead of 12, with 1 false alarm in 109 instead of 4. 0.50 would also lose the positive at 0.420.

Noul, text unchanged. Dev: TPR 0.60 (6/10), FPR 0.028 (3/108); four positives sit between 0.03 and 0.42, below any threshold that stays within 3%. Holdout: TPR 0.71 (10/14), FPR 0.047 (5/107). The unless on docs_only came from live use (2026-10-01): a commit of README and CHANGELOG alone scored 0.90 and was escalated, while documentation cannot change who gets in or what they can do. The bench numbers are the same with and without it.

Choice c_scelta, 1 − P(none). A note in NITS, never a block or an escalation. Dev: TPR 0.67 (8/12), FPR 0.019 (2/106). Holdout: TPR 0.81 (13/16), FPR 0.048 (5/105). The unless on docs_only came from live use (2026-10-04): two of the three false notes on 79 real commits of other repositories were documentation alone (a README with docs/ at 0.999, a CLAUDE.md at 0.94), while documentation cannot rename or remove what a caller uses. Without it the holdout FPR was 0.057 (6/105): one of its false notes was a docs-only diff; the positives are the same.

Choice c_scelta, 1 − P(none). A note in NITS. Dev: TPR 1.00 (7/7), FPR 0 (0/111). Holdout: TPR 1.00 (10/10), FPR 0.018 (2/111). Raised from 0.20 (2026-10-01), where the dev FPR was 0.027 (3/111) and the holdout's 0.072 (8/111): 0.76 is 0.20 on the Spark's calibrated scale, keeps every positive on both sets, and on 61 reviewed commits of this repository, which has no migrations, the note drops from 5 commits to none. The unless on docs_only came from live use (2026-10-04): a commit of CHANGELOG.md and docs/evaluation.md alone scored 0.997, the one docs-only diff among the three of 287 reviewed diffs that crossed 0.76, while documentation cannot rewrite or delete stored rows. Without it the holdout FPR was 0.027 (3/111): one of its false notes was a docs-only diff; the positives are the same.

Noul a_letterale. A note in NITS. Dev: TPR 0.88 (7/8), FPR 0.027 (3/110). Holdout: TPR 0.91 (10/11), FPR 0.036 (4/110). The unless on docs_only came from live use (2026-10-01): a commit of Markdown planning notes alone scored 0.81, while a debug leftover lives in application code. The bench numbers are the same with and without it.

Choice c_scelta sent as 'missing tests', reported as 1 − value: adds_tests ≤ 0.30 means missing tests with p ≥ 0.70. A note in NITS. Dev: TPR 0.74 (57/77), FPR 0.024 (1/41). Holdout: TPR 0.83 (50/60), FPR 0.066 (4/61). The same numbers with and without the unless on docs_only, which removes docs-only diffs: in both sets none of them crosses the threshold.

lanes._description_matches: description_matches is no longer in a rule: on the 2026-09-26 bench no wording goes above AUROC 0.662 (logit mean of two questions), and the checks.json text scores 0.426, worse than chance. It stays in checks.json as an informational question: its value is shown, the verdict does not depend on it.

band._comment: Escalation when |logit(p) − logit(threshold)| ≤ delta for a rule without an action on a critical check, chunk by chunk. Rules with "action": "escalation" have no band: their threshold is already chosen for few false alarms, and a band would add items below the threshold. In the plugin default every critical rule has the escalation, so the band applies to whoever moves a model rule back into a lane. 0.62 is the width of the old 0.35–0.65 band around 0.5.

escalation._hook: What the commit hook does with an escalation. deny_then_allow: the first attempt denies with the prompt for Claude, who rereads the listed files; the second, with the same diff and the same items, goes through without asking the user (the lane decides) and leaves a line in the log. The go-ahead applies only to the model's escalations (reason threshold or band): if the items include a detector (CI workflow, invisible characters, text addressed to the reviewer), a file the model did not see (minified, generated, binary, omitted) or a detector the model contradicts, the user decides on the second attempt. deny_then_ask: the second attempt always asks the user. context: no deny, the escalation only goes into Claude's context. The project can only tighten (context < deny_then_allow < deny_then_ask). BLOCK floors always deny.

ci._comment: neutral does not block the merge even with a required check: it applies only to a backend that is down, unreachable or not configured. Everything the author of a PR controls gives untrusted_input.

limits._comment: total_ms counts from the start of the hook, git commands included. For hook and skill, validation requires total_ms ≤ the hooks.json timeout (180 s) − 20 s.
